current_instruction: Continue planning before building. No installation, native engine implementation or compilation is authorized by this document itself.

creation_workflow.requirement: The three workflows must cooperate on one project. None is removed from the target.

planned_interpretation: Author and edit freeform mesh objects
Excavate caves and edit volumetric regions
Construct, dismantle and modify structures under game rules
Generate and revise assets and behaviors with AI
Extend systems through visual logic, scripts and native code
world_building.delivery_rule: Stages introduce working subsets while preserving the broader destination. The initial repair demo is not the complete building specification.

adam.personal_foundation: Adam is the creator's brother and safe person. This is the creator's story, using his brother's memory as the guide in the game.
adam.characterization_policy: The creator's memories guide the portrayal, including warmth, humor, encouragement and safety. Separate sourced recollections and historical quotations from newly written game dialogue.
adam.direction: Adam anchors the entire architecture as the internal compass and living core of AI-BS, connecting structural continuity, meaningful memory, authoring and gameplay.
adam.first_contact: I’m here. Start with what still responds.
adam.connection_verified: That connection holds. We can build from here.
adam.implementation_status: PROPOSED: required native continuity core at M2/M3, asynchronous provider enrichment at M5.

decisions.recommendation: Generic engine supplies registration, actions, events, assets, construction interfaces and scheduling. First Boot-specific faults, power rules and story live in its game module.
decisions.acceptance: Build and package a second mechanically different game without editing generic engine source.

decisions.recommendation: Use a versioned project manifest and shared scene/prefab/asset/behavior definitions across AI, visual tools and code. Maintain separate authoring, Play and saved-player states.
decisions.acceptance: Each authoring route opens the same entities and registered behavior bindings; stopping Play does not silently rewrite authoring.

decisions.recommendation: Versioned typed operations include operation ID, expected revision, preconditions, affected IDs/bounds and inverse information. A grouped scene operation validates and applies atomically. Committed operation results and deltas are recorded together.
decisions.acceptance: Retry a committed placement without duplicate entities or costs; reject an invalid grouped operation without partial changes; undo restores references and game resource state.

decisions.recommendation: AI produces inspectable change sets, generated assets or source patches. Scene changes use ordinary transactions; source patches use staged files and ordinary compile/validate/preview. Preview and automatic draft application are configurable product modes.
decisions.acceptance: An AI-authored scene edit appears in visual tools and undo history; generated source compiles through the same SDK build as handwritten source.

decisions.recommendation: Begin with prefab-local IDs, per-instance UUID maps, one base variant and explicit field overrides. Record override provenance and report conflicts after base updates. Add nested/structural variants after basic identity/undo behavior is proven.
decisions.acceptance: Duplicate a multi-object prefab with remapped internal references; update its base without losing valid instance overrides.

decisions.recommendation: Use registered typed actions/events/components for visual logic and scripts; native C++ extends systems. Preserve visual graph source and expose native functions as nodes, without claiming arbitrary C++ converts to a graph. Lua remains a later researched candidate, not an installed scripting backend.
decisions.acceptance: Equivalent visual and scripted interactions emit the declared events and save the same progression. A native extension registers a new typed action and inspector metadata.

decisions.recommendation: Layer modular/prefab objects, editable mesh objects, broad heightfield surfaces and localized sparse volumetric regions. Keep volume source semantics explicit: density and signed-distance fields are distinct choices.
decisions.acceptance: Place a module, reshape an object, sculpt a surface and excavate a cross-chunk tunnel; each introduced mode supports matching collision, undo and reload.

decisions.recommendation: Persist authored and created UUIDs, owning-cell IDs, creation records, deletion tombstones, terrain source edits and generator/content versions. Start with frozen unloaded simulation and explicit unavailable references.
decisions.acceptance: Create and delete objects, edit ground, unload/reload and restart without duplicates, resurrected deletions or lost edits.

decisions.recommendation: Prepare geometry/collision revisions off-thread and admit a matching ready revision at a simulation boundary. Dirty navigation tiles remain unavailable until the appropriate obstacle update or source-geometry rebake completes. Discard stale job results.
decisions.acceptance: Build a bridge, walk across it, admit rebuilt NPC routing, remove it and save/reload. A stale rebuild never replaces a newer edit.

decisions.recommendation: Share placement and geometry services. Editor tools retain structural validation and may bypass game economy/reach checks; player construction follows the game's registered cost, support, ownership and collision policies.
decisions.acceptance: The same recipe is placeable in the editor while an in-game attempt can fail with a clear resource/support/reach reason.

decisions.recommendation: Define forward PBR opaque/alpha-test/transparent passes, material and shader variants, basic culling/instancing, immutable render snapshots and bounded upload/remesh queues before high-detail mutable worlds.
decisions.acceptance: Construction, deletion and region transitions retain measured frame/memory budgets, and released content returns toward the established memory baseline.

decisions.recommendation: R0 foundation, R1 playable systems, R2 hybrid creator alpha, R3 editable streamed worlds, R4 reusable engine beta. Every tier has demonstrable creator/player outcomes and carries deferred target capabilities forward.
decisions.acceptance: Two distinct projects export offline packages; AI, visual and code authoring are each exercised before claiming the creator alpha.

decisions.recommendation: Implement AIBS::Adam as required native identity, semantic memory, evidence-backed interpretation, restoration-sensitive planning and expression across authoring and player contexts. AdamAnchor binds scene lore/presentation; model providers enrich an already-present core.
decisions.acceptance: Recall real choices, shortcuts and hazards after durable save/reopen offline; keep timeline branches scoped; commit memory with world deltas; play First Boot cues only from valid outcomes; presentation settings do not erase continuity.

open_design_items.details: Choose resource, support, dismantling, damage and structural-collapse policies for First Boot; keep generic policy interfaces reusable.
Choose density versus signed-distance semantics, chunk resolution, meshing/seam/LOD scheme and persistence after a budgeted editing prototype.
Choose initial event/condition/action graph serialization, node typing, cycle/loop rules, debug stepping and scripting backend/version.
Declare mesh/texture/rig/animation providers, accepted formats, generated-asset provenance and validation criteria; source images alone do not define these outputs.
Specify visual references, material/light/geometry budgets, animation count and minimum player hardware after measured native rendering.
Specify authored-world updates versus player modifications, conflict handling, migrations and rollback/export behavior.
Choose SDK/editor support policy, exact dependency versions and selected distribution terms during implementation planning.
Select authored voice direction, motif assets, caption pacing and real-device haptic patterns while preserving Adam's stable identity and accessible cues.
Define which real AI-BS development records become versioned First Boot lore, and any explicit narrative policy for recalling alternate attempts without presenting them as current-world facts.
